attempts.entry_title: Brain-wide mouse electrophysiology during eyepuffs and ketamine (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001326, which holds Neuropixels recordings of 13 sessions from 10 mice during eyepuff and tone series before and after ketamine, and the behavior in dandiset 001347. The first notebook covers the response clusters and their regional distribution, regional rise and decay times, the emotion-like population dimension and its first-order model, the fast and persistent coding dimensions with their baseline timescale and coupling, the tone responses, and the resting correlation structure and spectra. The second covers the eye closure of the recorded mice, the behavior-only mouse drug, dose, pressure and muscimol experiments, and the eye closure of four non-implanted participants, from dandiset 001347. The third covers the human iEEG factor analysis and the network cluster tests, from the derived spectrograms deposited in dandiset 001347.

outcomes.statement: Many thousands of single units were recorded across 13 sessions from 10 mice, with dozens of regions recorded simultaneously.
outcomes.source: Figure 4C; fig. S29A and S29B; table S2; table S3, Fig. 4E
outcomes.quote: We obtained recordings from many thousands of single units throughout the brain, with simultaneous recording of dozens of regions
outcomes.notes: 13 sessions from 10 mice, 9554 curated units, 6698 puff-modulated units (6491 if the code's minimum of 250 is read as spikes). The median session has units in 32 finest-level regions (range 11 to 37; 10 of 13 sessions have at least 24).
deviations: The units in the files are already curated (all labelled good, SNR at least 2.0, at least 517 spikes); the BombCell and ISI criteria cannot be re-applied, as the files hold no waveforms or ISI metrics.

outcomes.statement: Unsupervised clustering of peri-puff responses of puff-modulated units from all sessions gave twelve clusters spread over many regions, some responding rapidly and briefly and others persistently after rapid (clusters 0 and 1) or delayed (cluster 2) onset.
outcomes.source: Figure 4D and 4E; fig. S31A; table S3, Fig. 4E
outcomes.quote: Some clusters responded rapidly and briefly to the eyepuff whereas others responded persistently after either rapid (clusters 0 and 1) or delayed onset (cluster 2)
outcomes.notes: With scanpy's default Leiden seed and BLAS on one thread, 11 clusters (within one of 12). In descending order the sizes are 963, 772, 664, 657, 651, 604, 590, 579, 554, 491 and 173; 6 of the 12 expected sizes are within tolerance (the 3rd and the 8th to 11th are not) and there is no 12th (expected 176). By the criterion's measures (code find_decay, absolute values) clusters 9 and 6 are rapid and brief (decay 0.10 and 0.18 s) and two are persistent, cluster 0 (mean |1 to 2 s| 0.26 of the peak, peak at 0.11 s) and cluster 10 (0.42, peak at 0.77 s); the condition of three persistent clusters with two early peaks fails under both numberings. Clusters 1, 4 and 5 decay after 1.35, 1.16 and 1.24 s, with means over 1 to 2 s of 0.22, 0.14 and 0.18 of their peaks. Two of the 11 clusters (0 and 4) are suppressed. Over ten Leiden seeds the count is within 12 +- 1 in 6, 2 to 7 sizes are within tolerance, 0 to 3 clusters are persistent, and the full condition holds in none. The PCA in float64 gives 12 clusters with 7 sizes within tolerance, and the float32 PCA on 4 BLAS threads 11 clusters with 4 within (adjusted Rand index 0.71 against the main partition for both). Changed from partially reproduced after verification round 1: the cluster count holds but the sizes and the persistent structure, the substance of the claim, fail under every seed and both perturbations.
deviations: Leiden runs on the neighbor graph, as scanpy does and as the code calls it, not on the UMAP embedding the Methods name (criterion).
Peak, decay and the |z| < 1 rule follow analysis.py find_decay (plot_cluster_distribution), which works on absolute values; the criterion cites it.
Leiden's partition depends on its random seed; the default (0), which the code uses by calling sc.tl.leiden without one, decides the outcome, and ten seeds are shown.

The float32 PCA rounds differently with the number of BLAS threads, which changes the neighbor graph and the partition (1, 2 and 4 threads gave three partitions on the same data). BLAS is limited to one thread for the clustering so that the partition does not depend on the machine, a standard choice for a detail of computation; the float64 PCA and 4 threads are shown as perturbations.

outcomes.statement: Clusters overrepresented in the periaqueductal gray and VPM thalamus had fast, sharp responses, while clusters overrepresented in frontal cortex and limbic regions responded more slowly and persistently.
outcomes.source: Figure 4G; fig. S31A and S31B; table S3, fig. S31 B
outcomes.quote: Indeed, clusters overrepresented in midbrain (PAG) and thalamus (VPM) exhibited fast and sharp response dynamics, whereas clusters overrepresented in frontal cortex and limbic regions responded more slowly and persistently following the eyepuff
outcomes.notes: Default seed, BLAS on one thread. 54 regions have more than 30 clustered cells. Under the criterion's ranking (find_decay on the cluster mean of z-scored cells; faster half 2, 6, 7, 8, 9) the condition holds at FDR 0.05 and 0.01: PAG is overrepresented in cluster 9, VPM in clusters 2 and 8 at 0.05 and in cluster 8 at 0.01, and frontal or limbic regions in slower-half clusters (at 0.01 ACAv5, AId5, ORBl5 and PL2/3 in cluster 0, ORBvl2/3 in 1 and 5, ORBvl5 in 3 and 5). ACAd5 (both thresholds) and PL5 (0.05) are also overrepresented in the faster-half cluster 2. Under the ranking by the pooled baseline-subtracted trace of Fig. 4G (faster half 1, 6, 7, 9, 10) VPM is in no faster-half cluster, and the condition fails at both thresholds. Over ten Leiden seeds the criterion's ranking holds in 8 seeds at 0.05 and 7 at 0.01, the pooled ranking in 3 and 2, and all four combinations in 2 (seeds 4 and 8); every failure is the VPM part, while PAG and frontal hold in every seed. Chance is 1/11 here against the paper's 1/12. Changed from reproduced after verification round 1, and kept: the VPM part depends on the ranking and on the partition.
deviations: With 11 clusters the faster half is taken as the 5 fastest by find_decay.
Leiden seed and BLAS threads as for fig4de-response-clusters; ten seeds shown.

outcomes.statement: Ketamine substantially changed the responses of clusters with slow, persistent preinfusion dynamics but left fast clusters little changed.
outcomes.source: Figure 4G; fig. S31C; table S3, Fig 4G
outcomes.quote: Clusters with more rapid preinfusion dynamics were minimally altered or unaltered by ketamine, whereas clusters with slower and more persistent preinfusion dynamics were substantially altered

Over ten Leiden seeds no correlation is positive with p < 0.05 (rho -0.297 to 0.224 for the cosine distance, -0.486 to 0.248 for the difference).

outcomes.statement: Most regions responded to the puff with fast rise times, and ketamine did not change regional rise times.
outcomes.source: Figure 4I; fig. S31D to S31F; table S3, Fig. 4H, I
outcomes.quote: On a regional basis as well, the rise times of average neural activity were not altered by ketamine
outcomes.notes: 35 regions pass at the d' threshold 1.3 and 31 at 2. The median over regions of the bootstrap median change in rise time is +0.0001 s (Ketamine 23 to 32) or -0.0030 s (22 to 32) under every setting, within one 10 ms bin of zero. The Pre median rise is below 0.1 s in 32 of 35 and 30 of 31 regions. The more-than-30 and at-least-30 rules give the same regions. In the code's weighting a cluster without a value (peak after 750 ms) adds zero; that weight averages 0.089 of a region in Pre and 0.246 under ketamine. With the weights renormalized over clusters with a value, with Pre from series 11 to 20 only (20 replicate puffs, as Ketamine), or both, the change is +0.0065, -0.0040 and +0.0040 s, all within one bin, and the Pre rise is below 0.1 s in 31 to 35 regions. Bootstrap seed 0 is a standard choice.
The renormalized weights and the 10-series Pre set are verification controls, not the paper's method; the code's nansum weighting decides the outcome.

Sorted, they agree with the stimulus table: the population response 0 to 200 ms after each puff is 0.03 to 0.19 z in every session and -0.03 to 0.003 at onsets shifted by 1.5 s.

The animal excluded from the paper's Figure 5 and 6 analyses (Harderian gland secretion) is not identified in the dandiset or the paper. Removing sub-1, sub-3 or sub-5 each leaves 11 sessions from 9 mice; only removing sub-5 also leaves 7 tone sessions from 7 mice as table S3 reports, and several outcomes depend on the choice.

Question for the paper's authors. Which animal was excluded from the cross-puff and population analyses (Figs. 5 and 6, fig. S34)? This attempt assumes sub-5 (both sessions), the only choice that gives the 7 tone sessions from 7 mice of table S3; fig6d, fig6h, figs34d and figs34g change outcome if sub-1 or sub-3 was excluded instead.

Question for the paper's authors. Fig. 4B and 5B normalize each condition's mean eye-closure trace by its own maximum in analysis.py; is that the normalization behind the reported reduction? Without it, or with both conditions divided by the Pre maximum, the late closure of the recorded mice does not differ between Pre and Ketamine (0.026 [-0.030, 0.082]).
Tone series are in 9 sessions from 8 mice, where table S3 reports 7 sessions from 7 mice, and 9 sessions also hold light stimuli (240 to 248 per session) that the paper does not describe.

The ketamine infusion time in each file is described as approximate and falls 94 to 420 s after the code's ketamine onset (30 s after the last puff of series 20); with the code's onset, the tenth pre-infusion tone series counts as post-infusion.
867 of 9554 units carry the region label NA, and the files give no description of the region labels beyond the acronyms.
DANDI 001326 holds no eye closure; the recorded mice's eye closure is in DANDI 001347, with no file for sub-3_ses-20230225, sub-5_ses-20230706 or sub-5_ses-20230822, and with no tone events.

In DANDI 001347 the behavior-rig files hold only an eye-closure trace and an experiment id, with no drug, dose, pressure or injection label, and the human P50 files label trials only as pre and post. The conditions come only from the session lists of the paper's code (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.14920570).

The recorded-mouse eye-closure files of DANDI 001347 (sub-m<mouse>-<recording>) carry no identifier of the 001326 sessions; the link comes from the paper's conversion script and a clock fit to the series onsets.
Lick data (fig. S4), participant reports (Fig. 1F) and CADSS scores (Fig. 2D, fig. S14G) are not in DANDI 001347 or the code archive.

Table S3 gives a saline late eye closure of 0.34 for fig. S2C; the data give 0.203 while reproducing the table's t value (4.951) exactly, so the reported mean appears inconsistent with the reported test.

Table S3 gives 64 Ketamine puffs per cluster for Fig. 4G (8 series), while analysis.py takes series 23 to 32 (10 series); the recorded-mouse files of DANDI 001347 store a Ketamine range of series 23 to 30, which matches the table.

The coupling loop of analysis.py plot_coding_dimension_early_late takes the windows before puff series 1 to 10 and 23 to 32 whatever the stimulus, so the tone coupling of fig. S34H is computed before puff series, not before tone series as the Methods say; only that version shows a significant fall here.

In the 9 sessions with tones and lights, light or tone onsets fall in the 30 s before 14 of the 30 puff series that the baseline timescale and coupling analyses use (Pre 4 to 9 and 14, 16, 20; Ketamine 24, 28, 29, 30, 32), and in sub-1_ses-20230226 and sub-3_ses-20230225 light onsets fall in every odd 50 s post-series window. The paper does not mention the lights or say whether these windows were excluded.

The "Ketamine infusion start" of every file falls exactly 5.0 s before the first puff of series 21 (series 23 starts 235 to 266 s after it), so the stored infusion time appears to be placed from the puff schedule; its description says only that it is approximate.

The derived human files (sub-H) hold the inputs of the paper's factor and cluster analyses, and an NMF recomputed from sub-H_ses-sgramPerChannel with the paper's code settings gives back the deposited loadings exactly. The factor order of sub-H_ses-sgramNMFFactors is not the code's order by peak time (its factors 2 and 3 are swapped), and the files do not say which order the figures use.

entries.name: 001326-kauvar-2025
entries.title: Brain-wide mouse electrophysiology during eyepuffs and ketamine (Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Kauvar, Richman, Liu et al. (2025) on dandiset 001326, which holds Neuropixels recordings of 13 sessions from 10 mice during eyepuff and tone series before and after ketamine, and the behavior in dandiset 001347. The first notebook covers the response clusters and their regional distribution, regional rise and decay times, the emotion-like population dimension and its first-order model, the fast and persistent coding dimensions with their baseline timescale and coupling, the tone responses, and the resting correlation structure and spectra. The second covers the eye closure of the recorded mice, the behavior-only mouse drug, dose, pressure and muscimol experiments, and the eye closure of four non-implanted participants, from dandiset 001347. The third covers the human iEEG factor analysis and the network cluster tests, from the derived spectrograms deposited in dandiset 001347.
